examples.en: As the protests grew, the president stepped down from power.
He changed as soon as he rose to power.
To hold on to power, they pushed through unreasonable policies.
It isn't easy to resist the temptation of power.

examples.ko: 권좌로 가는 길은 생각보다 훨씬 험했어요.
examples.en: The road to power was much rougher than expected.

examples.ko: 권좌까지 오르는 데 이십 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took twenty years to climb all the way to power.

explain: 그냥 '자리'가 아니라 권력의 가장 높은 자리를 가리켜요. '권좌에 오르다/앉다', '권좌에서 물러나다/쫓겨나다'처럼 말하고, 일상 대화보다 뉴스나 역사 이야기에 나와요.

phrases.en: He rose to power at a young age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 높은 권력의 자리를 차지한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means taking the highest seat of power.

phrases.example: 권좌에 앉은 뒤 사람이 완전히 변했어요.
phrases.en: After taking the seat of power, he changed completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오르다'보다 이미 그 자리에 있는 상태에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses more on already holding the position than '오르다' does.

phrases.en: The king was driven from power by a rebellion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘으로 억지로 물러나게 되는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is forced out of power.

explain_en: It refers to the highest seat of power, not just any position. It appears in phrases like '권좌에 오르다/앉다' (rise to/take power) and '권좌에서 물러나다/쫓겨나다' (step down/be driven out), mostly in news and history rather than daily talk.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 도굴된 유물이 돌아왔다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the news that relics stolen from graves were returned to the museum.

examples.ko: 옛 무덤은 도굴 때문에 많이 훼손됐어요.
examples.en: Many old tombs were badly damaged because of grave robbing.
They installed CCTV at the historic site to prevent looting.
In the movie, the main character visits a looting site.
Cultural assets lost to looting are hard to recover.

examples.ko: 그 지역은 도굴이 자주 일어나서 경비가 강해요.
examples.en: Looting often happens in that area, so security is tight.

explain: 무덤이나 유적을 몰래 파서 물건을 가져가는 일이라 주로 뉴스, 역사, 문화재 이야기에서 나와요. '도굴하다', '도굴되다'로도 쓰고, 일상에서는 '무덤을 파헤치다'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The person who looted the old tomb was caught.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도굴'이 일 자체라면, 이 동사는 몰래 무덤을 파서 물건을 가져가는 행동을 직접 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Where 도굴 names the act, this verb describes the action of secretly digging up a tomb and taking things.

phrases.en: This ancient tomb was looted long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무덤이나 유물이 도굴을 당했다는 피해의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the passive form, used when the tomb or relics are the victims.

phrases.en: Grave robbers dug up tombs in the mountains at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도굴을 하는 사람을 가리키는 말로, 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to the people who rob graves and often appears in news or history stories.

explain_en: It mostly appears in news, history and talk about cultural assets. It is also used as '도굴하다' and '도굴되다', and in daily talk people may spell it out as '무덤을 파헤치다'.

examples.en: The criminal escaped the law and fled abroad.
The legal net is tight, so it's hard to slip through.

examples.ko: 그는 결국 법망에 걸려 처벌을 받았어요.
examples.en: He was finally caught by the law and punished.
Some people cleverly exploit the loopholes of the law.
This case exposed the gaps in the legal net.
There are still many people who slipped through the law.

explain: 법을 그물에 비유한 말이라서 '법망을 피하다', '법망을 빠져나가다', '법망에 걸리다'처럼 그물에 어울리는 동사와 같이 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 나오고 일상 대화에서는 드물어요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 법망을 피해 도망 다니고 있어요.
phrases.en: That person is on the run, evading the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그물을 피하듯 법의 처벌을 피한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like dodging a net, it means avoiding legal punishment.

phrases.example: 나쁜 사람들이 법망을 빠져나가면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Bad people must not slip through the net of the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법에 걸리지 않고 벗어난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means escaping without being caught by the law.
phrases.en_equiv: to slip through the legal net

phrases.en: That company was finally caught by the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그물에 걸리듯 법에 잡힌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like being caught in a net, it means being caught by the law.
phrases.en_equiv: to be caught by the law

explain_en: It pictures the law as a net, so it goes with net-like verbs such as '법망을 피하다', '법망을 빠져나가다' and '법망에 걸리다'. It appears often in news articles but rarely in everyday conversation.

examples.ko: 정치인이 비리를 저지른 부하를 비호하고 있어요.
examples.en: The politician is shielding a subordinate who committed misconduct.

examples.ko: 회사가 잘못한 직원을 비호해서 사람들이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: People got angry because the company protected an employee who did wrong.

examples.ko: 잘못한 친구를 무조건 비호하면 그 친구에게도 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: Defending a friend who did wrong no matter what isn't good for that friend either.

examples.ko: 누가 그 사람을 비호했는지 아직 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: We still can't tell who protected that person.
It's hard to trust articles that cover for the powerful.
The teacher didn't cover for the student who lied.

explain: 잘못이 있는 사람을 감싸고 지켜 줄 때 써서 '보호하다'와 달리 부정적인 느낌이 강해요. 사람이나 단체를 목적어로 해서 '~을/를 비호하다'로 써요. 일상에서는 '감싸 주다', '편들다'를 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 회사가 문제를 알면서도 직원을 비호해 줬어요.
phrases.en: The company knew about the problem but still protected the employee.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙여 누군가를 위해 감싸 준다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 주다 gives the sense of shielding someone on their behalf.

phrases.example: 범인을 비호하는 사람도 조사를 받아야 해요.
phrases.en: People who protect the criminal should also be investigated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못한 사람을 감싸 주는 사람을 가리킬 때 이렇게 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: This describes a person who covers for someone who did wrong.

phrases.example: 친구가 잘못했는데도 계속 편들면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't keep taking your friend's side when he is in the wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비호하다'보다 가볍고 일상적이라서 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is lighter and more everyday than 비호하다, so it sounds more natural in conversation.

explain_en: Unlike '보호하다' (protect), it carries a strongly negative feel, as it means shielding someone who has done wrong. It takes a person or group as the object: '~을/를 비호하다'. In daily speech people more often say '감싸 주다' or '편들다'.

examples.en: The police dragnet is closing in.

examples.ko: 범인은 수사망을 피해 계속 도망 다녔어요.
examples.en: The culprit kept running to avoid the dragnet.

examples.ko: 수사망에 걸린 사람이 벌써 세 명이에요.
examples.en: Three people have already been caught in the dragnet.

examples.ko: 이번 사건은 수사망을 넓혀서 다시 조사하기로 했어요.
examples.en: For this case, they decided to widen the dragnet and investigate again.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 수사망 밖에 있어서 아무 일도 없었어요.
examples.en: He was outside the dragnet, so nothing happened to him.
The news said the dragnet has spread across the whole country.

explain: '수사망이 좁혀지다', '수사망을 피하다', '수사망에 걸리다'처럼 짝말로 외워 두면 좋아요. 뉴스와 기사에 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '경찰이 쫓고 있어요'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: When the dragnet closed in, the culprit turned himself in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범인을 잡을 가능성이 점점 커진다는 뜻으로, 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the chance of catching the culprit keeps growing; very common in news.

phrases.example: 그는 몇 달 동안 수사망을 피해 숨어 지냈어요.
phrases.en: He hid for months, evading the dragnet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경찰이 쫓는 것을 피해 다닐 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for avoiding the police search.

phrases.en: The thief was finally caught in the dragnet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경찰이 쫓던 사람이 잡히거나 발견될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone the police are chasing is caught or found.
phrases.en_equiv: to be caught in the dragnet

explain_en: It is good to learn it in set phrases such as '수사망이 좁혀지다' (the dragnet closes in), '수사망을 피하다' (avoid the dragnet) and '수사망에 걸리다' (get caught in the dragnet). It appears a lot in news and articles, while in daily talk people say things like '경찰이 쫓고 있어요' (the police are after him).

examples.en: After the ports opened, new foreign goods and ideas came in quickly.
He was a person very interested in new foreign things.
The speed of accepting new things differed by country.
At the museum I saw an exhibit introducing new imported things.
People at the time found the new things amazing.
Western innovations changed daily life a lot.

explain: 주로 역사 이야기에서 새로 들어온 외국의 기술, 제도, 물건을 가리켜요. 요즘 나온 신제품에는 잘 쓰지 않고, '신문물을 받아들이다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: That country accepted new foreign culture quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 들어온 기술이나 제도를 받아들일 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for accepting newly introduced technology or systems.

phrases.en: He first came into contact with new foreign culture while studying abroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 문물을 처음 만나 보는 경험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the experience of first encountering new things.

phrases.example: 청년들은 서양의 신문물을 배우고 싶어 했어요.
phrases.en: Young people wanted to learn the new Western ways.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 새로운 지식과 기술을 익히려는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In history talk, it describes learning new knowledge and technology.

explain_en: It mostly appears in history talk for newly arrived foreign technology, systems and goods. It is not used for today's new products; a typical phrase is '신문물을 받아들이다'.

examples.en: Our troops crossed the bridge first.
It was hard to tell friend from foe in the movie.
In the game, I took the role of supporting my teammates.
They say our side's losses were smaller than expected.
We have to send a signal to our side.
The more allies you have at work, the better.

explain: 아군은 '적군'과 짝을 이루는 말이에요. 전쟁이나 게임에서 같은 편을 가리키고, 일상에서 같은 편이라는 비유로 쓸 때도 있어요. 평소에는 '내 편'이라고 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: In the game, allies and enemies are told apart by color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '적군'과 함께 짝으로 가장 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often appears paired with its opposite, 적군.

phrases.en: I helped my teammates in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임에서 같은 편을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for teammates in games.

phrases.en: In this matter, you're on my side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 같은 편이라는 뜻으로는 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life this is the more common way to say someone is on your side.

explain_en: '아군' is the pair of '적군' (enemy forces). It means your own side in a war or a game, and sometimes figuratively your allies. In daily talk people say '내 편' (on my side) more often.

examples.en: The army pulled out of that region completely.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 한국 시장에서 철수할 거예요.
examples.en: That company will withdraw from the Korean market.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 공사 팀이 일찍 철수했어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the construction crew packed up early.
It's dangerous, so workers, pull out of the site!
The firefighters went in through the people who were pulling out.

examples.ko: 경기가 나빠서 매장을 닫고 철수하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Business was bad, so they decided to close the store and pull out.

explain: '철수하다'는 군대나 회사, 팀이 있던 곳에서 물러날 때 써요. 일상에서 사람이 자리를 뜰 때는 '나가다', '떠나다'가 더 자연스러워요. 반대로 새로 들어가는 건 '진출하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The government pulled the army out of that area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이나 군대를 물러나게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making others withdraw.

phrases.en: The army withdrew from that area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 쉬운 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly easier similar word.

phrases.en: The commander gave the order to withdraw.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대나 현장에서 물러나라고 지시할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an order to pull out in the military or on site.

explain_en: 철수하다 is used when an army, company, or team pulls out of a place. For an ordinary person leaving a spot, 나가다 or 떠나다 sounds more natural. The opposite, moving into a new place, is 진출하다.

dis.h: pull out by itself, no object

p.n: 철수시키다 needs an object, so it does not fit a sentence where the subject itself withdraws.
